title: How the First Letter was Written

topics.name: As soon as / No sooner ... than / Hardly ... when

questions.rule: With direct speech use said (told needs a listener). After can, use the base verb draw.

options: Tegumai broke his spear, but he did not had another one.
Tegumai broke his spear, but he did not have another one.
Tegumai broke his spear, but he not have another one.
questions.rule: In this compound sentence, the second clause needs did not + base verb: did not have.

options: Taffy asked the stranger if did he know where her mother lived.
Taffy asked the stranger if he knew where her mother lived.
Taffy asked the stranger that he knew where her mother lived.
questions.rule: A reported yes/no question uses if and statement order: if he knew.

options: As soon as Teshumai saw the picture, she scream.
As soon as Teshumai will see the picture, she screamed.
As soon as Teshumai saw the picture, she screamed.
questions.rule: Both actions happened in the past, so both verbs are simple past: saw ... screamed.

options: Tegumai told Taffy not to disturb the stranger.
Tegumai told Taffy don't disturb the stranger.
Tegumai said Taffy not to disturb the stranger.
questions.rule: A negative command is reported with told + person + not to + verb.

options: The stranger smiled because of he had a daughter of his own.
The stranger smiled because he had a daughter of his own.
The stranger smiled because he have a daughter of his own.
questions.rule: Because (not because of) introduces a clause; he takes had in the past.

options: No sooner did the stranger left than Taffy sat down, pleased.
No sooner had the stranger left than Taffy sat down, pleased.
No sooner had the stranger left when Taffy sat down, pleased.
questions.rule: The pattern is No sooner had + past participle ... than.

options: Taffy said that I had drawn the spear outside our cave.
Taffy said that she had drew the spear outside their cave.
Taffy said that she had drawn the spear outside their cave.
questions.rule: In reported speech I/our become she/their, and had takes the past participle drawn.

questions.rule: An hour ago is past time, so use the simple past: broke.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Verbs joined by and keep the same tense: sat ... began.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After the past verb asked, the reported question moves back a tense: if he knew.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Got is past, so the main clause is past too: he ran.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The subject of are going needs the subject pronoun: Daddy and I.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The reported clause needs a subject pronoun: she had drawn it (Taffy's 'I' becomes she).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both clauses of this compound sentence are in the past: did not understand ... smiled.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Hardly pairs with when; than goes with no sooner.
After a quotation, use said. Told needs a listener, and spoke does not introduce words.

questions.after: the stranger saw the drawing, he nodded very hard.
questions.rule: As soon as shows that one action follows another immediately.

questions.after: the stranger to fetch the spear.
questions.rule: A request is reported with asked + person + to + verb.

questions.before: Tegumai had forgotten to bring extra spears,
questions.after: he had to mend the broken one.
questions.rule: The second clause is the result of the first, so join them with so. 'Because of' and 'despite' cannot start a clause.
'What have you been doing?' reported after asked moves back: what she had been doing.

questions.before: No sooner had the ladies seen the stranger
questions.rule: No sooner is always followed by than.

questions.after: was made of wood, broke in the river.
questions.rule: A spear is a thing, so the relative clause begins with which.

questions.before: The stranger wondered why the Chief
questions.rule: A reported thought after the past verb wondered takes the past perfect: had not noticed.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with direct speech.
questions.rule: Speaker + said, then the exact words inside quotation marks.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with 'As soon as'.
questions.rule: As soon as + first action, then a comma and the next action.
Reported request: asked + person + to + verb.
Main clause + subordinate clause of time beginning with before.
Hardly had + subject + past participle ... when + simple past.

chat: What did your teacher say today?
options: She said that the test were on Monday.
She said that the test was on Monday.
She told that the test was on Monday.
questions.rule: Use said that (told needs a person); the test is singular: was.

chat: Call me when you finish your drawing.
options: Sure, I will call you as soon as I will finish.
Sure, I am call you as soon as I finish.
Sure, I will call you as soon as I finish.
questions.rule: A future time clause uses the simple present: as soon as I finish.

chat: Did you finish the letter to Grandma?
options: Yes, I wrote it, and Dad post it this morning.
Yes, I written it, and Dad posted it this morning.
Yes, I wrote it, and Dad posted it this morning.
questions.rule: Both clauses of this compound sentence are in the simple past: wrote, posted.

chat: What did the new boy ask you?
options: He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where I live in.
questions.rule: A reported wh-question uses statement order and shifts back: where I lived.

options: No sooner had we left home than it started raining.
No sooner we had left home than it started raining.
No sooner had we left home when it started raining.
questions.rule: No sooner had + subject + past participle ... than.

chat: What did Ms Iyer tell you after class?
options: She told me to bring my art book tomorrow.
She told me bring my art book tomorrow.
She said me to bring my art book tomorrow.
questions.rule: Reported instruction: told + person + to + verb. Said cannot take me directly.

options: I missed the bus, so I have to walked.
I missed the bus, so I had to walk.
I missed the bus, so I had walk.
questions.rule: Past necessity: had to + base verb (walk).

chat: Did the match start on time?
options: Hardly we had sat down when the first ball was bowled.
Hardly had we sat down than the first ball was bowled.
Hardly had we sat down when the first ball was bowled.
questions.rule: Hardly at the start needs inversion (had we) and pairs with when.

options: Taffy said that I was happy.
Taffy said that she were happy.
Taffy said that she was happy.
questions.rule: I becomes she and am becomes was.

questions.prompt: Combine into a compound sentence using 'but'.
questions.source: The stranger smiled. He did not understand a word.
options: The stranger smiled, but he did not understand a word.
The stranger smiled, but he not understand a word.
The stranger smiled, but he does not understood a word.
questions.rule: Two main clauses joined by but; keep did not + base verb.

questions.source: Tegumai said to Taffy, "Don't bother me."
options: Tegumai told Taffy not to bother me.
Tegumai told Taffy not to bother him.
Tegumai told Taffy to not bothering him.
questions.rule: Negative command: told + not to + verb; Tegumai's me becomes him.

questions.source: As soon as Taffy saw the carp, she stamped her foot.
options: No sooner did Taffy saw the carp than she stamped her foot.
No sooner did Taffy see the carp than she stamped her foot.
No sooner Taffy saw the carp than she stamped her foot.
questions.rule: No sooner needs inversion: did Taffy see (did + base verb) ... than.

questions.source: Taffy asked her father if he would be surprised.
options: Taffy said to her father, "Will he be surprised?"
Taffy said to her father, "Will you be surprised?"
Taffy said to her father, "Would you surprised?"
questions.rule: In direct speech Taffy speaks to her father: he becomes you and would becomes will.

questions.prompt: Make it a complex sentence using 'Because'.
questions.source: Taffy could not write, so she drew pictures.
options: Because Taffy could not write, so she drew pictures.
Because Taffy could not wrote, she drew pictures.
Because Taffy could not write, she drew pictures.
questions.rule: Because replaces so; never use both. After could not, use the base verb.

questions.source: The stranger said, "I will get help from the Chief's tribe."
options: The stranger said that I would get help from the Chief's tribe.
The stranger said that he will got help from the Chief's tribe.
The stranger said that he would get help from the Chief's tribe.
questions.rule: I becomes he and will becomes would.

questions.source: As soon as the stranger reached the cave, the ladies attacked him.
options: Hardly had the stranger reached the cave when the ladies attacked him.
Hardly the stranger had reached the cave when the ladies attacked him.
Hardly had the stranger reach the cave when the ladies attacked him.
questions.rule: Hardly had + subject + past participle (reached) ... when.
